newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CanWest offers to reduce Ten stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: CanWest offers to reduce Ten stake - paper.

text.p: Canada's CanWest Global Communications Corp has offered to sell down its stake in Australia's Ten Group Ltd to 57.5 percent, provided its holding is protected at that level, the Australian Financial Review reported on Friday.

CanWest is under pressure from the Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) to reduce its holding after the ABA found CanWest illegally controlled the television network through its 76 percent economic interest.
CanWest has rejected the ABA's findings, saying it has a voting interest of only 15 percent, in line with the approved limit.

The Financial Review said CanWest has lodged documents with the Australian government proposing to reduce its interest to 57.5 percent if the government "universally and unconditionally" provides grandfathering protection to its interest at that level.

The newspaper said CanWest contended it was entitled to retain its 76 percent interest under Australian and international law, but was prepared to sell down its stake given the sensitivity of the matter.
